value.the_failure_mode_named: Structure measured when behaviour was meant. I read the guard, constructed a census by hand to test it, and never asked what root the LIVE caller passes — the one line (orient.py:121) that decides the whole question. A seeded control run under MY shape reproduced my own mistake faithfully and read as confirmation.
value.the_measurement_that_killed_it: device_census(root=Path('/home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn'))['measured']['components'] -> 26 device rows, 13 of them top-level and passing the guard. Seeded control under the LIVE shape: a fixture $T/devices/{a_fixture_device/thing.py importing cairn.devices.inference_domain, inference_domain/host.py} through device_isolation_holds({'dir':'devices/a_fixture_device',...}) -> n=1, about='a_fixture_device/thing.py imports [...] — a_fixture_device may not import inference_domain'. value.what_actually_stands: The sieve is healthy. What remains true from the cast is the OTHER half, and it was never this ticket's: cairn/machines/ is outside device_isolation_holds's reach by design (the guard is for top-level DEVICE rows), so nothing stops a file under cairn/machines/ from importing a device. That gap is 76639374d9f9's machine_imports_no_device piece and needs no ticket of its own.
value.why_it_is_false: THE CENSUS EMITS BOTH SHAPES, AND WHICH ONE DEPENDS ON THE ROOT. cairn/tools/orient/orient.py:121 — `root = root or (_REPO_ROOT / 'cairn')`. The LIVE inspector run (inspector.py:3313) takes that same default, so it censuses /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn and rows read 'devices/inference_domain' — two segments, and the guard matches. I measured with root=/home/akien/dev/src/cairn (the repo root, one level up), which is a legal call nobody makes, and rows came back 'cairn/devices/inference_domain'. The zero was mine, not the sieve's.
